amount: US$5,000 or US$10,000 grants (about £4,000 to £7,700) plus mentoring
good: Social impact ventures led by young founders, with grants and mentoring.
name: MoveNow Social Innovation Challenge 2026
view: Share with young social-impact founders in our network, alongside UnLtd.
when: Open now; closes 18 December 2026 (exact time not given).
who: Founders aged 18 to 30, anywhere in the world, running a social impact venture.

good: Small projects that improve Bristol city centre: experiences and promotion, safe communities, clean and welcoming streets, or green ideas.
name: City Innovation Fund (2027 projects)
view: Share with TWEA founders based in central Bristol; it is a weak fit for TWEA itself because events are unlikely to be funded.
when: Open now until 31 January 2027 (the closing time is not given). Applicants meet the panel in early February and projects run from 1 April to 31 October 2027.
who: People and organisations in, or delivering projects in, the Bristol BID area. Levy payers come first. Events are unlikely to be funded.

amount: €22,000 grant per start-up, plus accelerator support; 20 places
good: Start-ups that bring together sustainability, good design and inclusion, in climate, food or urban mobility.
name: Catalyse NEB 2027
view: Share with TWEA founders working on climate, food or transport who also care about inclusion and design.
when: Opened 26 October 2026 and closes 15 January 2027 at 5pm CET (4pm UK time).
who: For-profit start-ups set up after 1 January 2022 in an eligible country, including the UK, with some revenue or investment and under €1m raised.

amount: Up to €850,000 per project (EIT Health pays up to half of costs)
good: Clinical validation, regulatory filings and launch preparation for digital and AI medical technology that is nearly ready for market.
name: Innovation Validation Call 2027
view: Share with TWEA health tech founders, including those joining the Boston mission, who need clinical evidence.
when: Opened 14 October 2026 and closes 13 January 2027 at 3pm (time zone not stated, so check the funder's page).
who: Groups of at least two organisations from different countries, led by a company selling the product. UK organisations can take part.

amount: Cash prizes, no equity taken (amounts not confirmed)
good: Global pitch competition with Idea, Early, Growth and AI tracks; finals in Saudi Arabia.
name: Entrepreneurship World Cup 2027
view: Share with founders who want pitching practice and Middle East exposure; could pair with a TWEA pitch clinic in spring.
when: Open now; closes 31 May 2027 (exact time not given).
who: Startups under 10 years old from any country, team members 18+. No application fee.

amount: €10,000 per grant (about £8,700); 1 to 5 grants this round. €50 application fee, which can be waived
good: Equity-free grants to help early-stage founders reach a milestone, such as a launch, testing demand or growth.
name: Forward Grant (October–December 2026 round)
view: Share with women of colour founders in our community and at our clinics; a good fit for our inclusive-access work.
when: Open now; closes 31 December 2026 at 11:59pm Central European time (10:59pm UK time).
who: Women of colour founders aged 18+ based in the UK or Europe, with businesses at least 50% women-owned. Idea stage to early revenue.

amount: Projects of £150,000 to £250,000, up to 70% funded; £3.1m in total
good: Feasibility studies for frontier AI in health, advanced materials, defence, and AI safety.
name: Frontier AI: SME Champions, Phase 1
view: Too late for this round; keep an eye out for Phase 2 and tell our AI founders when it opens.
when: Closes 11 November 2026 at 11am, too soon to act on. A Phase 2 may follow.
who: UK-registered small and medium-sized businesses applying alone. Not charities.

amount: Two-day bootcamp and coaching; no cash stated
good: Pitch, go-to-market and investor-meeting coaching for a cohort of 10–15 start-ups before Web Summit Qatar 2027.
name: Road to Web Summit Qatar 2027
view: Not for us: it appears limited to start-ups already in Qatar's own programmes.
who: Start-ups already in Qatar's national innovation and entrepreneurship programmes.

amount: £100,000 – £200,000 grant per project; up to £5m per strand
good: Helps a small AI company test its working product with a bigger business or public body, ending in a real-world demonstration.
name: BridgeAI Deployment Catalyst, Phase 1 (three strands)
view: Share with TWEA founders who already have a working AI product and a big customer ready to trial it; the deadline is close.
when: Opened 21 October 2026 and closes 8 December 2026 at 11am. There are three strands: Operational Systems, Assurance and Compliance, and Decision Critical Systems.
who: A UK small business with a working AI product leads, teamed with one medium or large business or public body in a key sector. It pays 40–70% of costs.

amount: Over S$2.5 million (about £1.4m) in prizes in total; finalists flown to Singapore
funder: Singapore Management University (Institute of Innovation & Entrepreneurship)
good: Deep-tech startups in climate, energy, food, urban mobility, health and sustainable materials; route into an accelerator and fund.
name: Lee Kuan Yew Global Business Plan Competition 2027
view: Share with university spin-outs and graduate founders via UWE, Bristol and Bath universities; also a useful Asia link for our trade missions.
when: Opened 29 October 2026; closes 31 March 2027 (exact time not given, so check the funder's page). Finals in Singapore, 28 September to 1 October 2027.
who: Startups with at least one founder still at university or who graduated in the last 5 years. Open to founders worldwide.

amount: Top prize US$250,000 cash (about £190,000) plus US$1m in Azure credits; smaller prizes for 2nd, 3rd and a student prize
good: Software startups in areas such as developer tools, health, fintech, cyber security, retail and deep tech or physical AI.
name: Imagine Cup 2027
view: Share with our youngest software and AI startups; worth flagging at the next founder clinic as a pitching practice target.
when: Opened 2 November 2026; closes 28 February 2027 at 11:59pm US Central time (early on 1 March UK time). Entries are reviewed as they come in.
who: Registered startups founded on or after 2 November 2024 that have not raised Series C. Founders 18+. Needs a Microsoft for Startups account.

amount: US$100,000 – US$125,000 per fellow (stipend plus US$25,000 project budget); 10 places
good: A year-long paid fellowship for people building trustworthy, public-interest technology, either hosted by a partner or working independently.
name: Mozilla Fellowships 2027–2028
view: Share with TWEA founders and members working on responsible AI who could step away for a year.
when: Letter of intent due 17 December 2026 at 11:59pm US Pacific time (7:59am UK time on 18 December). Fellowships start 1 June 2027 for 12 months.
who: Individuals from any background who can legally receive Mozilla funding. Hosted places are in Indonesia, Chile, Germany, the US and Nigeria, or remote.

amount: US$300,000 for the first year, up to US$500,000 over three years (no equity taken)
good: Community-centred AI projects built on small, fit-for-purpose models that are already in use by the people they serve.
name: Incubator 2027: Human-Scale AI cohort
view: Tell TWEA founders building small, privacy-friendly AI for communities straight away; there are only days left.
when: Closes 20 November 2026 at 11:59pm US Pacific time, which is 7:59am UK time on 21 November. Decisions by February 2027; support starts April 2027.
who: Teams worldwide with working technology and a charitable purpose; money must be able to flow from a US charity (fiscal sponsors allowed). Not frontier-model chatbots.

amount: £3m programme in total; grant sizes not published
funder: The National Lottery Community Fund · UK Community Foundations · CAST
good: Helps community organisations shape and build their own AI tools, to close the gap between AI and local know-how.
name: Community Powered AI
view: Ask Quartet Community Foundation whether the West of England is part of this pilot and if TWEA could join with a local charity.
when: No open application found. The pilot will back about 50 community organisations, with first grants expected from autumn 2026.
who: Community organisations in the UK; how to apply has not been published.

good: Workshops, drop-ins and one-to-one help so people feel confident using digital tools.
name: Digital Inclusion Fund
view: Not open now. If TWEA confirms a not-for-profit structure, watch for the next round as a small pot for an inclusive digital skills session.
when: The 2026 round ran 6 October to 3 November and is now closed; it may come back.
who: Not-for-profits (charities, community groups, CICs, social enterprises) that help SNG customers and communities, including in Wiltshire.

amount: Free cohort place; no cash grant (no fee stated)
good: A 16-week course for business leaders putting AI into important systems: picking the use, planning, launching and checking results.
name: Practitioners Hub: AI Deployment Studio
view: Share with TWEA founders and scale-up leaders who are about to roll out AI in their business.
when: Registration opened 4 November 2026 and closes 30 November 2026 at 11:59pm. The 16-week cohort runs from 7 January to 22 April 2027.
who: Senior leaders at a UK-registered company in one of the eight Industrial Strategy sectors that plans to use AI in a business-critical area. No technical knowledge needed.

amount: No cash: two years in the World Economic Forum community, with events and profile
good: Recognition and global network for about 100 early-stage tech companies a year.
name: Technology Pioneers 2027
view: Share with our strongest scale-ups, especially those in the GTA Innovation Funding Working Group pipeline.
when: Open now; closes 31 January 2027 (exact time not given, so check the funder's page).
who: Early-stage technology companies worldwide with a strong product and growth story. Details to be confirmed on the WEF site.

amount: €75,000 per startup (about £65,000), plus mentoring and coaching
funder: European Innovation Council (Horizon Europe) · Women TechEU
good: Early-stage, women-led deep-tech startups: equity-free funding plus a business support programme.
name: Women TechEU 2026–27
view: Share with women-led deep-tech founders in our network now, so they have time to pass the eligibility check before January.
when: Next full-proposal deadline is 14 January 2027 at 4pm UK time; later rounds close in May and August 2027.
who: Startups 6 months to 5 years old, registered in the UK or EU, with a woman founder in a top role and women owning at least 25%.
